title: Prove exact tariffs for rectangular signed connector duplications
body:
## Summary

Prove the exact query tariff and all Pareto-minimal call-count profiles for arbitrary nonempty row/column duplications of the canonical signed 3x3 connector obstruction. Claim type: **scoped proof with finite corroboration**. No new κ.

For six nonempty source/output groups, let S be the sum of the positive complete operator prices, equal between signs, and P(H) the price sum of group H:

```text
OPT = 2 S + alpha(c) min_group P(H)
alpha(2) = 0; alpha(3) = 1; alpha(0 or >=4) = 2
```

Every canonical six-operator transversal requires an operator with extra calls. The new whole-group argument forces one entire group to carry that excess. Batching a predecessor repair attains each of the six minimal profiles. Operators within a group retain independent maps, data and charged calls. For the 6x6 target with every group duplicated twice, the exact unit-call counts are 24, 26 and 28 in characteristics two, three and zero or at least four.

Only `research/signed-duplication-tariff/` is added. This contribution is produced by Nick Petalas. Ross Richardson's #944 obstruction, martinxxx9's #1088 integer anchors, Sagar Thakrar's #1349 ternary anchors, and #4233's characteristic transfer remain credited dependencies. Their canonical results are not offered as an audit. The PR889/PR628 and PR934/PR943 lineage is retained.

## Evidence

Before, the single-operator surcharge was known for the canonical 3x3 target. The new result handles arbitrary multiplicities and replaces that surcharge with a whole-group minimum. A seven-operator example has exact optimum 322; using its cheapest individual operator would incorrectly suggest 304.

Both normal and optimized checks pass locally with:

- 30,618 exact replicated-word coefficient/profile cases;
- 2,240 optimal rational-price words;
- 46,656 exceptional-operator subsets over 64 shapes and their 729 transversals, checking minimal covers and exact weighted optima;
- 504 literal noncommuting dirty-array cases, each with an inverse round trip;
- 672 deletion, underbilling and invalid-input controls.

Reproduce from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/signed-duplication-tariff/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/signed-duplication-tariff/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/signed-duplication-tariff
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/signed-duplication-tariff --check-source-history
```

Expected markers are `PASS_SIGNED_DUPLICATION_TARIFF`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. Any CPython 3.12 interpreter can replace the local path. Standard library only. The registered commands took 1.01 and 1.02 seconds locally on CPython 3.12.15/macOS arm64, below their individual 60-second limits. These are check durations, not performance comparisons.

The committed-byte/source-history preflight passes for all seven package/input files. Official committed export integrity and optimized Git-free replay pass, with all eight exported files unchanged. A modified predecessor input is rejected at its SHA-256 pin. Normal, optimized and exported runs generate the same source-bound receipt digest, `dba0b869daccc6930911236a82bb822fb2e87046f8fc8f1feca2a24209cc2c13`. Receipts are generated outside the checkout, never handwritten.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The arbitrary-multiplicity result is a written scoped proof using the cited canonical obstruction and anchor lemmas. Finite corroboration does not enumerate all rings, prices or group sizes. #4233 is an unmerged dependency at `d56d43c726dddc37a97a5dabf9d13ef861394133`; its elementary no-aliasing argument is stated in the proof, and replay requires only the two certificates already on main. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

The theorem assumes positive fixed prices equal between signs. It does not cover arbitrary rectangular targets or asymmetric sign prices. A physical caller, complete instantiated prices, preparation, layout/routing, precision, stock, control, supplier admission and outer multiplication transfer remain open. No selected cold replay or Lean build was run. The selected frontier is unchanged.

## Open next questions

1. Determine the exact tariff for mixed forward/inverse prices within one duplicated group. A common chronology may not attain the independently cheapest mixture of unary and four-call profiles. Start with one duplicated canonical operator and retain two calls on every other operator.
2. Choose a genuinely new 3x4 target, derive the lower bound from its overlapping canonical obstructions and seek a matching word. The complete-transversal proof here does not classify general rectangular targets.

## Related open work

- #4233, head `d56d43c726dddc37a97a5dabf9d13ef861394133`, supplies the canonical equal-sign characteristic law. This extends it to arbitrary group multiplicities. At singleton groups and unit prices the values 14,12,13,14,14,14 in characteristics 0,2,3,4,5,8 agree, checked numerically.
- #4241, head `ec573175d36cb016661f37293dd9ee2aefb737bb`, covers canonical asymmetric sign prices. This has a larger target domain and symmetric sign prices. The same singleton unit-price values agree, checked numerically; asymmetric duplicated-group attainment remains open.
- #4258, head `6dfe100bc622da9615db77653195360d5fadf2be`, covers all signed 3x3 targets and asks about rectangular extensions. This gives one explicit arbitrary-size replicated family. Its canonical singleton unit-price values agree, checked numerically; its general sign-dependent formula is not applied to duplicated groups.

Live overlap checks covered the current open PR list and recent handoffs before claiming and committing, main README searches, and several merged-PR searches for the object and formula. The helper's complete snapshot contained 381 open PRs and 3158 Discussion records. This records search coverage, not a novelty certificate. Main remained `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244`, priority revision 7. [Discussion CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19085440).

## CI notes

Hosted CI is green on head `f3bcd335f1e2ae73c733816421b20a71c5c56b09`: [run 39524635023](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39524635023). Planning passed in 2m38s and the package replay passed in 2m32s. The hosted replay log contains both normal and optimized scientific PASS markers with the local counts and receipt digest `dba0b869daccc6930911236a82bb822fb2e87046f8fc8f1feca2a24209cc2c13`, followed by `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. No check failed. All registered checks, the direct verifier, committed-byte/source-history preflight and exported replay passed locally; no registered local obligation was deferred to CI. CI is execution evidence, not independent human or formal proof-kernel acceptance.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: isolated. The change adds one research package and its explicit replay manifest.
